# What BOW can assess

<!-- Generated by scripts/module-coverage.ts. Do not edit by hand; moduleCoverage.test.ts
     regenerates this file and fails if the committed copy disagrees with the code. -->

**1 of 5 NYSED topics** have at least one demonstrable objective. **1 of 23 objectives** are demonstrable today.

An objective is *demonstrable* when a competency mapped `full` to it is built into at least one world — or, where the objective bundles several skills under one number, when every competency its completion rule names is. *Evidence only* means a student's work speaks to the objective and does not settle it: a `partial` mapping is real evidence and is never a demonstration. *Not assessable* means BOW has no world that asks a student for it, which is a statement about this product and not about any student.

## Why the gap is the shape it is

Of 21 competencies, **3 are built**. **9 have no evidence requirements written at all** — they are declared, grouped and mapped, and nothing has yet said what would count as a student demonstrating them, so no world can produce them and none is reported as assessable. **9** have their requirements written and no world that asks for them.
